title: Quasi-solitons of the 1D Bose gas at arbitrary-strength contact repulsion
authors: Anahita Sarvi, Cesare Vianello, Jean-Sébastien Caux
abstract: Harnessing integrability at arbitrary interaction strength, we build long-lived and spatially localized soliton-like excitations in the 1D Bose gas with contact repulsion (Lieb-Liniger model). We show how these density profiles, built from selective superpositions of multi-hole eigenstates, display long lifetimes tunable through parameters like dispersion width and number of holes. We further illustrate a scaling protocol that in principle enables unbounded increase in lifetimes in the thermodynamic limit. Our results showcase classical-like excitations originating from unitary quantum dynamics, away from the semi-classical regime, and in regions where interactions cannot be treated perturbatively.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to study quasi-solitons in the 1D Bose gas at any interaction strength using the Lieb-Liniger model. By selectively superposing multi-hole eigenstates, the authors show how to create robust, localized excitations whose dynamics are governed by unitary quantum mechanics. This advances understanding of non-perturbative quantum behavior in strongly correlated quantum gases.
main_problem: The study focuses on constructing and analyzing long-lived, spatially localized, soliton-like excitations (quasi-solitons) within the one-dimensional Bose gas.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that by using a selective superposition of multi-hole eigenstates, they can generate such quasi-solitons with long lifetimes, even in the strongly interacting regime where perturbative methods fail.
method: The methodology involves constructing time-evolving wavefunctions as superpositions of Bethe Ansatz eigenstates and calculating the time evolution of the density profile using specific matrix elements.
model_or_system: The system is the 1D Bose gas interacting via a contact repulsion, modeled by the Lieb-Liniger Hamiltonian. The analysis utilizes the exact solvability provided by the Bethe Ansatz.
key_observables: Density profile $\rho(x, t)$, and lifetime quantified by time power series $\Delta\rho(t)$ and depletion integral $R(t)$.
important_parameters: Arbitrary contact repulsion strength ($c$), number of holes ($n$), and system size/density ($N/L$).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is the applicability of the Bethe Ansatz framework to build the required quantum states, allowing the study beyond the semi-classical or weak-coupling limits.
figures_summary: Figures compare analytical and numerical results for density matrix elements and the 1-hole density profile in the Tonks-Girardeau (TG) regime, confirming theoretical predictions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general Hamiltonian formulation to the construction of wavepackets using multi-hole states. It then details the calculation of density matrix elements and concludes by verifying the expected fixed-point density in the TG limit.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantum mechanical treatment of classical-like excitations (solitons) in a strongly interacting quantum gas, extending beyond the standard Gross-Pitaevskii mean-field approximation.
